persons.name: Heisenberg
persons.digest:
Heisenberg mostly walked through the post-election picture and his earlier calls. He said possible deadlocks in 2027 budget talks could raise volatility, which does not mean a falling market but may create a need for hedges such as option spreads.

He pointed out that **BIST 100** fell to the support he flagged in September and that **oil** saw $30-40 targets at the bottom and now $200 targets in what he sees as a distribution phase, so he is leaning against the crowd on both. The rest of his posts were about the X environment, subscriptions and arguments, so I left them out.

persons.name: ulkser
persons.digest:
Serkan Uelker said outright that he bought a first tranche of gold and silver; he sees no bottoming signal, added **gold** and **silver** as precious metals to his portfolio and will buy separately lower down. He also described doubling money in 4 days on option-heavy **QXO** and **RKT** and leveraged **QQQ**/**IWM** trades, and said he is taking profits.

He finds the post-election selloff in AI and Musk companies overdone: he calls the selling of **TSLA** and **SPCX** and the crushing of chip and memory names curious, and says **DRAM**, **SMH** and **NCLD** are still not cheap but are nearing bounce levels. In his view these will not lead this period; he expects the reaction to fade within a week.

persons.name: Ahmet Sunelcan
persons.digest:
Ahmet Sunelcan reads today's post-election drop almost entirely as an AI selloff: he writes that the market is pricing that no new data centers can be built so **MSFT**, **AMZN** and **META** capex will fall, calling it a once-in-40-years kind of confusion. In his view it is an AI bear market with other areas in a bull market, and bulls should stay away from AI.

In his own portfolio he said he increased **FPS** and that he will publish the portfolio after the close.
